title: Honest Interval Radius for Coarsened Exact Matching with Empirical-Quantile Bins and Pruning
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: subfield < field; paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4. Not salvageable within scope — bank downgraded, or re-anchor the proposal.
gap_reasons: Its significance remains bounded by the scalar, exactly uniform covariate experiment, fixed overlap, binary outcomes and deterministic public group-size family, which do not characterize general CEM inference.

The finite certificate returns the entire interval [-1,1] for every sample size up to 2000, and the package supplies no implemented or demonstrated useful finite-sample calibration, limiting its practical bin-choice contribution.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the matched finite honest-width frontier for the actual empirical-quantile CEM center, including the critical logarithm and every-public-q randomized-radius converse; a headline arithmetic error was repaired and independently adjudicated. The final mathematics and decision panels passed, and four source citations were independently attested, but the general panel capped the package at subfield (6.8 versus 7.4) for structural scope and vacuous small-sample calibration. The operator-required below-field stop ended the run before Lean formalization; a materially broader future re-anchor may reuse the analytic results.
tldr: For the prescribed empirical-quantile CEM center, the optimized finite \(0.90\)-honest worst-class expected interval length is of order \(\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+[\log(\mathrm e+n)/n]^{\alpha+\beta}\}\). A total original-record radius and a public logarithmic group rule attain this bound. Same-class displacement constructions obstruct every public group size and every randomized honest radius, even when inference uses discarded records. Root-sample-size precision holds exactly when \(\alpha+\beta>1/2\); the equality case has the necessary factor \(\sqrt{\log n}\).
gap: Ghosh--Wang, Section 5, identifies finite bin choice as unresolved. Partition-mass concentration does not quantify within-group arm-selection covariance or the causal effects lost through pruning. Gaussian conditional bias-aware inference and dense propensity subclassification solve different decision problems.
fill: Conditional arm coefficients yield a finite calibration using both nuisance moduli. Same-class displacement constructions must obstruct every public \(q\), including merged residual and single-group partitions. Matching those directions determines a numerical frontier and the exact precision region.
